On the morning of her first infusion, Elena arrived at the clinic forty minutes early and sat in the waiting room with her hands folded around a paper cup. She had read the consent form three times. The nurse who greeted her was kind in a practical way, explaining each step before she did it: the IV line, the monitor, the little button to press if anything felt wrong. Elena nodded at everything. Over the next two hours the drip ticked steadily and she watched the clouds move past the window, thinking about her daughter, about the diagnosis, about the odd fact that she might be helping someone she would never meet. When the bag was empty, the nurse squeezed her shoulder and said, "One down." It was the first time in months that the future had felt like something she could count.
